title: Top Processes widget
line: There is now a ready-made Top Processes widget that lists the processes using the most CPU, with their memory use.
explanation: Plasma had ready-made System Monitor widgets for CPU, memory, disks and network, but none for processes: you had to add a System Monitor widget and switch it to the Process Table style yourself. Presets also could not set up a face's own options, because SensorFaceController::loadPreset read the FaceConfig group through a file key that applet packages don't define, so it always found nothing (since 2020). The libksysguard change reads FaceConfig from the preset's faceproperties file, and plasma-systemmonitor gains a "Top Processes" preset (next to the Process Table face it uses) that shows all processes, sorted by CPU, with Name, CPU and Memory columns.

commits.message:
faces: apply the face settings stored in presets

Presets keep their face settings in the FaceConfig group of their
faceproperties file, but loadPreset looked them up with a file key that
applet packages don't define, so those settings were always ignored.

BUG: 443373

presets: add a Top Processes widget

There was no ready-made widget to show which processes use the most
resources. This adds a System Monitor preset using the Process Table
face that lists all processes by CPU use, with their memory use.

BUG: 443373

Subject: [PATCH] faces: apply the face settings stored in presets

Presets keep their face settings in the FaceConfig group of their
faceproperties file, but loadPreset looked them up with a file key that
applet packages don't define, so those settings were always ignored.

BUG: 443373
---
 faces/SensorFaceController.cpp | 2 +-

diff --git a/faces/SensorFaceController.cpp b/faces/SensorFaceController.cpp

+++ b/faces/SensorFaceController.cpp
@@ -950,7 +950,7 @@ void SensorFaceController::loadPreset(const QString &preset)

     if (d->faceConfigLoader) {
-        KConfigGroup presetGroup(KSharedConfig::openConfig(presetPackage.filePath("FaceProperties"), KConfig::SimpleConfig), QStringLiteral("FaceConfig"));
+        KConfigGroup presetGroup(c, QStringLiteral("FaceConfig"));
 
         for (const QString &key : presetGroup.keyList()) {
             KConfigSkeletonItem *item = d->faceConfigLoader->findItemByName(key);
--

From 4db798ca57831ccb2cf7cf60281ae66767cc78ab Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 23:10:00 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] presets: add a Top Processes widget

There was no ready-made widget to show which processes use the most
resources. This adds a System Monitor preset using the Process Table
face that lists all processes by CPU use, with their memory use.

BUG: 443373
---

 src/presets/CMakeLists.txt                    |  1 +
 .../contents/config/faceproperties            | 10 +++++++
 src/presets/topprocesses/metadata.json        | 29 +++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 41 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 src/presets/CMakeLists.txt
 create mode 100644 src/presets/topprocesses/contents/config/faceproperties
 create mode 100644 src/presets/topprocesses/metadata.json

diff --git a/src/CMakeLists.txt b/src/CMakeLists.txt
index 6c77a8b1..e1542e7f 100644
--- a/src/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/src/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 add_subdirectory(page)
 add_subdirectory(table)
 add_subdirectory(faces)
+add_subdirectory(presets)
 
 
 add_definitions(-DQT_NO_KEYWORDS)
diff --git a/src/presets/CMakeLists.txt b/src/presets/CMakeLists.txt
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..2862be8e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/presets/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+kpackage_install_package(topprocesses org.kde.plasma.systemmonitor.topprocesses plasmoids plasma)
diff --git a/src/presets/topprocesses/contents/config/faceproperties b/src/presets/topprocesses/contents/config/faceproperties
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..1f749492
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/presets/topprocesses/contents/config/faceproperties
@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+[Config]
+chartFace=org.kde.ksysguard.processtable
+
+[FaceConfig]
+userFilterMode=3
+sortedColumns=name,usage,memory
+columnWidths=0.5,0.25,0.25
+sortColumn=usage
+sortDirection=1
+columnDisplay={"name":"text","usage":"text","memory":"text"}
diff --git a/src/presets/topprocesses/metadata.json b/src/presets/topprocesses/metadata.json
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..44de4a6d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/presets/topprocesses/metadata.json
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+{
+    "KPackageStructure": "Plasma/Applet",
+    "KPlugin": {
+        "Authors": [
+            {
+                "Email": "niccolo@venerandi.com",

+            }
+        ],
+        "BugReportUrl": "https://bugs.kde.org/enter_bug.cgi?product=plasmashell&component=System%20Monitor%20widgets",
+        "Category": "System Information",
+        "Description": "System monitor widget that shows the processes using the most CPU",
+        "EnabledByDefault": true,
+        "FormFactors": [
+            "desktop"
+        ],
+        "Icon": "view-process-system",
+        "Id": "org.kde.plasma.systemmonitor.topprocesses",
+        "License": "GPL-2.0+",
+        "Name": "Top Processes",
+        "Website": "https://www.kde.org/plasma-desktop"
+    },
+    "Keywords": "Processes;Top;CPU;Memory;",
+    "X-Plasma-API-Minimum-Version": "6.0",
+    "X-Plasma-Provides": [

media.caption: Widget explorer on master: searching "process" finds nothing.
With the fix: a "Top Processes" widget is offered.
Same preset with master's libksysguard: its face settings are ignored, so it shows own processes sorted by memory with every column.
With the fix: all processes sorted by CPU, with Name, CPU and Memory columns.
